meta.titre: Globalisation and its Effects: a connected world and its local consequences
meta.sous_theme: Meaning, causes, advantages and disadvantages of globalisation

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A young tailor in Douala posts photographs of her dresses on social media, receives an order from a customer abroad and is paid through a mobile money service within minutes. The same phone shows her the latest fashion from other continents, and some of her customers now ask for imported styles and not for the traditional fabric. This is globalisation at work, bringing both opportunities and worries. The GCE asks what causes it and what it does to the economy, society and culture, so you must be able to argue on both sides.

items: A country is an independent state with its own territory and government.
Trade is the buying and selling of goods and services.
Culture is the way of life of a people, including language, dress, food and beliefs.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning
Globalisation is the growing connection between countries and peoples of the world in trade, finance, communication, politics and culture, so that events in one place quickly affect people in many other places.

### Factors that favour globalisation
| Factor | How it links the world |
|---|---|
| Information and communication technology | The internet, mobile phones and satellite television carry news, money orders and ideas across borders in seconds |
| Faster and cheaper transport | Aeroplanes, container ships and better roads move goods and people between continents |
| Freer trade | Lower barriers and trade agreements, encouraged by bodies such as the World Trade Organization, let goods circulate more easily |
| Multinational companies | Firms that work in many countries spread products, jobs and technology |
| International organisations | The United Nations and regional bodies bring states together on common problems |
| Modern banking and payment systems | Money can be sent abroad quickly and safely |
| Travel, migration and study abroad | People carry their customs and skills from one country to another |

### Effects
| Field | Advantages | Disadvantages |
|---|---|---|
| Economic | Larger markets for exports such as cocoa and coffee, foreign investment, new jobs and technology | Cheap imports can ruin local producers, small countries depend on world prices, skilled workers may leave (brain drain) |
| Social and cultural | Quick access to information, online education, exchange of ideas and awareness of human rights | Local languages and customs can be forgotten, young people may copy foreign lifestyles, cybercrime and harmful content spread |
| Political and health | Cooperation against common problems such as disease and pollution | Diseases cross borders quickly, and powerful states can pressure weaker ones |

Globalisation therefore offers chances but also risks. Its results depend on how well a country prepares its people, protects its producers and keeps its own culture alive.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks what has made globalisation possible or easier
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the factor, then say how it connects countries, for example: 'The internet. It lets people in different continents trade, study and talk at once.' Do not give effects such as unemployment or loss of culture here, because they are results and not causes.

Group your points by field (economic, social, cultural) and, when the word 'discuss' is used, give at least one advantage and one disadvantage. An answer that shows only one side loses marks. Always explain the link between the cause and the effect.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how a country or a community can face the dangers of globalisation
variantes.contenu_markdown: Suggest measures: teaching and speaking mother tongues, wearing and promoting local clothes and foods, supporting local producers, educating young people to choose wisely what they watch and share online, and making laws against cybercrime.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the model answer to this question: Describe two benefits and two dangers of globalisation for a young Cameroonian who sells clothes online. [8 marks]

etapes.action: Read the command word and count the points required.
etapes.justification: 'Describe' wants a clear account of each point, and the question needs two benefits and two dangers, four points in all, each worth about two marks.
It sets the frame of the answer and earns a mark of understanding.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Globalisation is the growing connection between countries through trade, communication and culture.

etapes.action: Choose benefits linked to the seller's situation.
etapes.justification: Points must fit the case in the question and not be copied from a general list.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Wider market through the internet; fast payment and easy purchase of materials from abroad.

etapes.action: Choose two dangers that also fit the case.
etapes.justification: A balanced answer shows both sides of the topic.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Cheap imported clothes compete with the seller's prices; foreign fashion may reduce demand for local designs; online fraud.

etapes.justification: Each point needs a short reason, and the conclusion shows judgement.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Globalisation is the growing connection between countries through trade, communication and culture. For a young Cameroonian who sells clothes online, one benefit is a wider market: through the internet she can reach buyers far beyond her town and earn more. A second benefit is easy access to payment services and to materials or ideas from abroad, which improves the quality of her work. One danger is competition: cheap imported clothes can force her to lower her prices or lose customers. Another danger is the loss of interest in local designs, as young people copy foreign fashion, and the risk of online fraud. In conclusion, globalisation gives her real opportunities, but she must protect her business by keeping her designs original and by being careful online.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Globalisation is the use of the internet.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The internet is only one of the factors. Globalisation covers trade, finance, politics and culture as well.
items.correction_markdown: Globalisation is the growing connection between countries in trade, communication, politics and culture.

items.erreur_markdown: In a question on factors, a student writes 'unemployment and loss of culture'.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are effects, not causes of globalisation.
items.correction_markdown: Give factors such as information technology, faster transport, freer trade and multinational companies.

items.erreur_markdown: In a 'discuss' question, a student writes only about the dangers of globalisation.
items.pourquoi_faux: A discussion needs both sides. An answer with one side cannot earn full marks.
items.correction_markdown: Give advantages and disadvantages, then a short judgement.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Globalisation makes all countries equally rich.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Globalisation does not share wealth equally. Rich countries and large companies often gain more, and some producers lose.
items.correction_markdown: Globalisation can bring wealth, but gains and losses are not equally shared.

items.erreur_markdown: A student confuses globalisation with colonisation.
items.pourquoi_faux: Colonisation was the political control of a territory by a foreign power. Globalisation is the growing interdependence of free countries.
items.correction_markdown: Colonisation is rule by a foreign power; globalisation is the growing link between countries through trade, technology and culture.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Define globalisation. (b) Name three means by which people in different countries are linked today.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Globalisation is the growing connection between countries and peoples in trade, communication, politics and culture.** (b) Award a mark for each valid means, for example the internet, mobile phones, satellite television, air transport, container shipping, international banking, trade agreements.

items.enonce_markdown: A shop in a Cameroonian town sells imported shirts at 4,500 FCFA each, while a local tailor sells similar shirts at 6,000 FCFA each. A school club wants 40 shirts. (a) Calculate how much the club saves by buying imported shirts. (b) Explain one reason why buying only imported shirts could harm the local economy.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Cost of 40 imported shirts = 40 x 4,500 = 180,000 FCFA. Cost of 40 local shirts = 40 x 6,000 = 240,000 FCFA. Saving = 240,000 - 180,000 = **60,000 FCFA**.

(b) Award a mark for the point and a mark for its explanation. If customers buy only cheap imports, local tailors lose income and may close their workshops, so jobs are lost and money leaves the country. Local skills also disappear when there is no demand for them.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain how improved transport and communication encourage globalisation, and discuss two ways in which young Cameroonians can enjoy its benefits without losing their own culture.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for explanation and for discussion. Explanation: **faster transport (aeroplanes, container ships, better roads) moves goods and people quickly, so trade grows and countries become dependent on one another; communication (internet, phones, satellite) lets news, orders, money and ideas move in seconds, so markets, studies and friendships cross borders.** Discussion, two ways: **(1) use the internet to learn, sell and share local products while continuing to speak mother tongues and wear local dress at suitable occasions; (2) choose carefully what to watch and copy, keeping positive foreign ideas such as new skills while respecting the values and traditions of the community.** Other valid ways: supporting local producers, taking part in cultural festivals, recording elders' stories.

items_markdown: Globalisation is the growing connection between countries in trade, finance, communication, politics and culture.
Information technology, faster transport, freer trade, multinational companies and international organisations are factors that favour it.
Effects are both good (wider markets, jobs, information, exchange of ideas) and bad (ruined local producers, loss of culture, cybercrime, spread of disease).
Do not mix causes with effects: unemployment is an effect, the internet is a factor.
In a 'discuss' question give both sides and a short judgement.
A country can protect itself by teaching its culture, supporting its own producers and educating its youth to use technology wisely.
